title: From Enter to the page
instruction: Fill in what happens from pressing Enter to the finished page.
debrief: Every page is an exchange of requests and responses. First the name becomes an address, then comes the HTML, then everything the HTML points to.

items.text: You type our-club.org. Your computer knows only the name, but data needs {0}. The number comes from {1}.

options: DNS, the phone book of the internet

items.why: The name is for people, the IP address for the network. DNS translates one into the other.

items.text: The browser, the {0}, sends the server a {1}: send me the home page.
items.why: The client asks, the server answers. The language of that conversation is HTTP.

items.text: The request and the response travel split into {0}. They are passed on by {1}, each one a bit closer.
items.why: Each packet carries the address of its destination. When a router on the way fails, the others send the packet round it.

items.text: The server returns {0}. In it the browser finds links to CSS, scripts and pictures, and for each file it sends {1}.

options: a finished picture of the page

items.why: HTML is the skeleton of the page. A single news page can easily mean a hundred requests.

items.text: The page is put together from the files that arrived and drawn by {0}.
items.why: The server sends the material; your device puts the picture together. That’s why even a weak device can slow a page down.
